idiom_name: sealed token hierarchy + when or lambda table with binding powers
implementation_notes: Kotlin makes the token set a sealed hierarchy and the parselets lambdas - (Parser, Expr) -> Expr, or extension lambdas Parser.() -> Expr - so the class-per-parselet structure degenerates into a when over the token or a map lookup, and the grammar stays data. The Kotlin specification fixes precedence for Kotlin's own grammar through its productions (with an explicit note that conditional expressions behave specially), but the standard library provides nothing that parses expressions, so the loop is hand-written; if the grammar grows beyond expressions, a Kotlin-targeting parser generator or kotlin-parser is the alternative. Prefer an enum token kind plus when when exhaustiveness is the goal, and a Map<TokenKind, Rule> when operators register at runtime.
pitfalls: Map.getValue throws NoSuchElementException for a token with no registered handler, far away from the offending token; pre-build a rule for every token kind or check explicitly and raise a positioned syntax error.
Using KClass as the map key boxes and compares class references on the hot path; an enum token kind or a when over the sealed hierarchy keeps both speed and exhaustiveness.
Recursive descent exhausts the JVM stack on deeply nested input (StackOverflowError, typically without a usable position), so carry an explicit depth counter.
